subject: storytime
title: The Golden Goose
about: The Brothers Grimm's tale of a kind youngest son who shares his bread with a little gray man and is given a goose with golden feathers, and of the two sisters, the baker and the farmer who stick fast to it until a princess who never laughs sees the silly parade go by. First graders love the growing line of stuck people and the big laugh at the end, and the lesson is said plainly: kindness comes back to you. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Shout 'Stuck!' together each time someone grabs on, then count how many are in the parade.

book.author: the Brothers Grimm (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A golden goose, a line of stuck people, and a princess who finally laughs.

passage.text:
Once there was a man with three sons.
The two big brothers never shared a thing.
But the youngest son was kind.
One day, he went to cut wood.
He had only a bit of bread.
A little gray man sat under a tree.
"I am hungry," he said.
"Will you share your bread?"
"Yes," said the son.
"Sit down with me."
They ate the bread together.
***
"Thank you," said the little gray man.
"You shared, so I will share too."
"Cut down that old tree."
"You will find a gift in its roots."
The son cut down the tree.
In the roots sat a goose.
Its feathers were made of gold!
"A golden goose!" said the son.
He picked it up and set off down the road.
***
That night, he stopped at an inn.
Two sisters saw the golden goose.
"I want just one gold feather," said the big sister.
She touched the goose.
Her hand stuck fast!
The little sister tried to pull her off.
Now she was stuck too!
In the morning, the son set off again.
The two sisters had to go with him.
***
A baker saw them go by.
"Let me help you," he said.
He grabbed the little sister.
Stuck!
A farmer grabbed the baker.
Stuck!
Off they all went down the road.
Two sisters, a baker and a farmer, all stuck fast!
What a silly parade!
***
In that land lived a princess.
She was always sad.
She never, ever laughed.
"Who can make her laugh?" asked the king.
Then the silly parade came by her window.
The princess looked.
She giggled.
Then she laughed and laughed and laughed!
Pop! Everyone came unstuck.
The princess and the kind son became best friends.
Kindness comes back to you.

cards.q: What did the youngest son share with the little gray man?
cards.note: He had only a bit of bread, and he sat down and ate it together with the hungry little man.

cards.q: Where did the son find the golden goose?
cards.note: The little gray man told him to cut down the old tree and look in its roots.

cards.q: What happened when the big sister touched the goose?
cards.note: She wanted one gold feather, and her hand would not come off; her sister stuck to her next.

cards.q: Who laughed at the silly parade?
cards.note: She never, ever laughed, until two sisters, a baker and a farmer went by stuck to a goose.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The kind son shares his bread with the little gray man before anything else happens.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: After the big laugh, everyone came unstuck and the princess and the kind son became best friends.

cards.q: How did the princess feel before the parade came by?
cards.note: She was always sad and never, ever laughed, which is why the king wanted someone to make her laugh.
The son shared his bread, and the little gray man shared a golden goose right back.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'stuck fast' mean?
cards.note: Here 'fast' means held tight, not quick: the sisters, the baker and the farmer could not let go.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
